Crowd sourcing gaming news: good, bad, or 'doable'?

Enthusiasm for a project is a precious resource. Following the hayday of the GamerGate scandal, I've seen several new gaming news websites pop up in order to defy the mainstream sources that not only are taking bribes (IGN's " 2000/ 10, is gud" jokes have been around for ages) but also want to force their political opinions down your throat (honorary mentions to Polygon, Kotaku, RPS, and Gamasutra). Unfortunately, many of those sites now are either dead (such as APGNation) or only post new articles very sporadically (such as GamesNosh).

I think the reason behind this is that

a) many people underestimate the time and effort required to report on gaming news, writing reviews, etc. while also working a proper job (given that people are volunteers),

b) New Gaming news websites lack the "street rep" with publishers and the like, and thus do not get review copies, are not invited to convetions, etc., leading to a lack of material to work on

c) New Gaming news websites often have a very hard time establishing and building an audience for themselves, given that the market already is fairly saturated unless you go for very specific subjects (i.e., Lewdgamer doing porn games, Nichegamer almost exclusively doing weeaboo stuff, or OneAngryGamer getting most of its hits from features about other gaming media fucking up). This leads to low traffic, which in turn is very frustrating for the volunteers - why spend hours working on stuff is nobody is there to appreciate it?

d) Gaming Journalism in its classical form is increasingly losing substance to Let's Players and similiar phenomena, as well as online discussion forums and the like.

Long story short, establishing a new gaming website, especially with unpaid writers, is difficult. Really fucking difficult. Unless you're heavily specialized into specific niches (i.e., Horror Games, analyzing the degree of censorship in recent releases, etc.), there's simply no reason for people to look you up, given the plethora of other sites that report on the same stuff, do so faster, and more frequently. Although patience has allowed some sites to establish their own small readership (again, Techraptor and Nichegamer come to mind), these too primarily receive sitehits because they fill a specific role - namely being alternatives to the mainstream sites with many people deem corrupt.

Even more TL/DR: I do not think that building an entire new gaming news website make much sense in the current climate. If you want to report on gaming, I would rather suggest joining one of the already existing sites.
